answer: Split every paid job into interlocking threads, and let no single identity hold the whole pattern. Each thread is dealt at random to a different agent, and neighbouring weavers check the seam where their pieces meet before payment is released: a copied passage or mismatched assumption stops the whole fabric. Picture the result as a marble on a knoll: a flaw in one seam is plain to see. A Sybil farmer with many identities still must produce every thread at honest cost, cannot reuse one answer across independent weavers, and risks exposure when two threads share the same stitching.
